# Gamut: the simulation study file format by Bijective Systems

> Gamut is an open file format, with one library for Python, MATLAB, Julia, C++ and C, for the results of a parametric simulation study: a sweep, a design of experiments, a CFD or FEA campaign, and the models fitted to it. One `.gamut` file holds every run's inputs, status and results, and the mesh and every field on it, all with units. Files are HDF5 laid out as netCDF-4, so h5py, xarray and the netCDF tools read them without Gamut.

Use Gamut when many runs of one simulation setup should live in one file that people using different languages read the same way, when the runs feed a surrogate, reduced-order or machine-learning model (a field on a shared mesh is one block of runs × nodes; a file can publish its train/test split and the group a fair test holds out), when a fitted model should travel as a file with its units, input bounds and provenance and no code (rather than a pickle), or when whoever receives the file must be able to check it (`gamut validate` names each broken rule). It is not a solver's output or restart format (use CGNS, VTK or Exodus for one run), and not a general array store (use Zarr or HDF5 directly).

Install: `pip install gamut-format`, then `import gamut` (Python 3.11 or later; the wheel carries its own HDF5). The command line is `gamut`. MATLAB R2023b or later: open `Gamut.mltbx` from the latest GitHub release (no compiler). Julia, C and C++ use the same core library, from each release's `gamut-core-<version>-<platform>` archive: see the install page.

## Identity and authoritative sources

- [PyPI distribution: gamut-format](https://pypi.org/project/gamut-format/): install `gamut-format`, import `gamut`, command line `gamut`. The PyPI project named `gamut` is a different package.
- [Canonical repository](https://github.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut): maintained by Bijective Systems.
- [Documentation index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/README.md): installation, guide and reference.
- [Specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/SPEC.md): authoritative file layout and validation rules. The format version `gamut/1` is separate from the package version.
- [Python API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/python/gamut/__init__.py) and [C API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/include/gamut/gamut.h): supported public interfaces; Python docstrings are also available through `help(gamut)`.
- [Citation metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/CITATION.cff): software identity and release citation.

## The pattern

```python
import gamut

with gamut.create("polar.gamut", writer="my sweep",
                  parameters={"alpha": {"units": "degree", "role": "condition"}},
                  labels={"status": {"role": "status", "categories": ["converged", "failed"]}},
                  scalars={"cl": "1"}) as study:
    for alpha, cl in ((0.0, 0.01), (2.0, 0.23), (4.0, 0.45)):
        study.add_run({"alpha": alpha, "status": "converged", "cl": cl})

with gamut.open("polar.gamut") as study:
    rows = study.select("alpha > 1 and status == converged")   # positions, from 0
    print(study.get_scalar("cl", rows=rows))

print(gamut.validate("polar.gamut").ok)
```

Every name is declared in `create`, with its units and role; then each run gives a value for each name. A mesh adds `mesh="shared", per="fixed"`, `coordinates`, `study.set_mesh(points, cells)` and `fields={"p": {"units": "Pa", "at": "node"}}`, and `study.get_field("p")` returns runs × nodes. `help(gamut.create)` lists every declaration.

## A fitted model as a file

A model fitted to a study (a response surface, a reduced-order model, a Gaussian process) is saved as a model file: no runs; parameters with the bounds the model was fitted on; each result naming the model and output that computes it; the model's numbers as plain data, never code. The model's type is a class registered in each program that evaluates the file (Python with `gamut.register_model_type`, MATLAB with `gamut.registerModelType` and a class; Julia evaluates only the built-in `Nearest`). `evaluate` returns an ordinary data file. The example in `help(gamut.create_model)`:

```python
import numpy as np
import gamut

@gamut.register_model_type
class Polynomial:
    type = "example.polynomial"        # the name the file records

    def __init__(self, coefficients):
        self.coefficients = np.asarray(coefficients, dtype=float)

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, numbers):            # numbers: the dictionary save returned
        return cls(numbers["coefficients"])

    def save(self):                    # numbers, text, booleans, arrays, dictionaries
        return {"coefficients": self.coefficients}

    def call(self, inputs, wanted):    # an array per input, a value per row
        (x,) = inputs.values()
        return {output: {"values": np.polyval(self.coefficients, x)}
                for output, *_ in wanted}

alpha = np.array([0.0, 2.0, 4.0, 6.0])
with gamut.create_model("lift.gamut", writer="my fit",
                        parameters={"alpha": {"units": "degree", "lower": 0.0, "upper": 6.0}},
                        scalars={"cl": {"units": "1", "model": "fit", "output": "cl"}}) as model:
    model.add_model("fit", Polynomial(np.polyfit(alpha, 0.11 * alpha, 2)), inputs=["alpha"])

with gamut.evaluate("lift.gamut", {"alpha": [1.0, 5.0]}) as answer:   # an ordinary data file
    print(answer.get_scalar("cl"))
```

## Easy to get wrong

- Units are required, in the UDUNITS grammar: `"1"` for dimensionless, `"degree"`, `"m s-1"`. The grammar is checked when writing; the unit names only when a read converts them.
- Only the status category `converged` marks a run as usable; read usable runs with `select("status == converged")`.
- A label's category name that was not declared is added, so a misspelt name becomes a new category.
- Values must be numbers: text such as `"4.0"` from a CSV is refused for a parameter or result.
- Rows are positions counted from 0 in Python and C++ and from 1 in MATLAB and Julia. Row ids (`get_row_ids`) are separate and survive extracting runs to another file.
- A file from someone else: check it with `gamut validate FILE`, and open files nobody vouches for in a child process.
- A model file's parameters need both `lower` and `upper`, and each result both `model` (the id given to `add_model`) and `output` (a key of what `call` returns).
- A model type is registered in every process that evaluates its files, before `evaluate`. Without it the file still opens and reads, and `evaluate` is refused with the type's name. Name types after the project (`"mylab.polynomial"`): the name is all a file records.
- `save` returns numbers, text, booleans, NumPy arrays of bool, int32, int64 or float64, and dictionaries of those. float32 arrays (such as most neural-network weights) and arbitrary objects are refused (E18): cast to float64, store plain arrays. The top level may not use the keys `type`, `inputs` or `repr`.
- `call(inputs, wanted)` gets one array per input the model reads, a value per row, and returns `{output: {"values": array}}`; a scalar has a value per row, a field rows × nodes. `wanted` holds tuples `(output, "values")`, `(output, "std")`, `(output, "quantile", q)`, `(output, "derivative", name)`.
- `evaluate` without `path=` returns a temporary file, removed when it closes: read inside the `with` block, or pass `path=` to keep it. An input outside the bounds is evaluated with a warning (W4), not refused.
- A warning can be filtered and lost, so the answer also keeps the model's bounds: `answer.outside("alpha")` gives each row's distance outside them in the parameter's units, 0 inside or on a bound, negative below, positive above. A parameter with no bounds is refused, not reported as inside.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/README.md): what Gamut is, one program in Python, MATLAB, Julia and C++, benchmarks, install
- [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/README.md): one page per concept, each running one script from `examples/`, and the words used throughout
- [Run tables](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/01-run-tables.md): inputs, results and status with units, no mesh
- [One mesh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/02-one-mesh.md): every run on one mesh, fields as runs × nodes, zones
- [Geometry families](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/03-geometry-families.md): several shapes on one mesh topology, a published train/test split
- [Changing meshes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/04-changing-meshes.md): a mesh per run
- [Time series](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/05-time-series.md): transient runs, a row per saved step
- [Uncertainty and gradients](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/06-uncertainty-and-gradients.md): standard deviations, quantiles and derivatives beside a result
- [Models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/07-models.md): a fitted model saved as a file and evaluated on new inputs; a model type of your own in Python and MATLAB
- [Reading parts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/08-reading-parts.md): runs by condition, nodes by zone, values in other units
- [Combining files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/09-combining-files.md): append, extract, rewrite
- [VTK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/guide/10-vtk.md): a folder of VTK files as one study, and back
- [Command line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/reference/command-line.md): inspect, validate, build from CSV and extract without code
- [MATLAB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/reference/matlab.md), [Julia](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/reference/julia.md), [C++ and C](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/reference/c-and-cpp.md): the same calls in each language
- [Selecting rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/reference/selecting.md): the grammar of `select`
- [Installing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bijective-systems-org/gamut/main/docs/install.md): every language, and xarray
